drew-estate--liga-privada-no-9.description: Drew Estate's dark Liga Privada blend from Estelí, Nicaragua: a stalk-cut, stalk-cured Connecticut River Valley Broadleaf over a Brazilian Mata Fina binder, with Nicaraguan and Honduran filler. It takes its number from the ninth of the trial blends built around that leaf. Dense and oily, it smokes with cocoa, dark coffee and earth, and suits a slow evening.

thirds.notes: Soft cocoa and a caramel-like sweetness open, with bursts of pepper and a little spice.
The sweetness recedes; charred, grilled notes and coffee take over, with pepper and woody tobacco rising.
Leather and espresso lead to the end, with dark cocoa and clean pepper on the finish.

sources.title: The Cigar Authority – Liga Privada No. 9 review
Blind Man's Puff – Liga Privada No. 9 Robusto

drew-estate--liga-privada-t52.description: The second Liga Privada blend, wrapped in a Connecticut-grown Habano leaf that is stalk-cut, stalk-cured and rested for up to three years before rolling. A Brazilian Mata Fina binder holds Honduran and Nicaraguan filler. The profile is dry and earthy, with black pepper, cocoa and wood, and a slightly sweet finish.

thirds.notes: Oily earth and a strong pepper finish, with chocolate and cedar early before charred wood steps in.
Sweetness comes back as cocoa with a touch of cinnamon, over the same earthy core.
The sweetness falls away; wood and smooth earth remain, with a little coffee on a long finish.

sources.title: The Cigar Authority – Liga Privada T52 review
Cigar Obsession – Liga Privada T52 Robusto review

drew-estate--liga-privada-h99.description: The third Liga Privada blend, named for its H99 wrapper, a hybrid of Connecticut Corojo and the T52 Habano. A Mexican San Andrés binder holds Nicaraguan, Honduran and Pennsylvania Green River filler. It starts nutty and woody with baking spice, then grows into coffee, cedar and leather as the strength climbs to full.

thirds.notes: Wood, a salty nuttiness and baking spice, with cream and black pepper in support.
Coffee rises to join cedar and oak; pepper and spice build as the strength reaches full.
Darker and drier, with coffee, cedar and earth, closing on leather and a savoury edge.

sources.title: The Cigar Authority – Liga Privada H99 Toro review
Cigar Coop – Liga Privada H99 Toro review

drew-estate--liga-privada-10-aniversario.description: First shown in 2018 to mark ten years of Liga Privada, this blend wears a hybrid Connecticut Criollo wrapper over a San Andrés Otapan Negro binder, with Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania Green River filler. Oak, coffee and pepper lead, with a creamier, chocolate-and-nut middle and a leathery, peppery close.

thirds.notes: Oak and coffee bean up front, with earth, a hint of fruit and white pepper on the nose.
Rounder and creamier: coffee stays, joined by chocolate and nuts while the pepper eases.
Leather returns with lemon rind, and pepper builds again over charred oak.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Liga Privada 10 Aniversario Toro review
The Cigar Authority – Liga Privada Aniversario Robusto review

drew-estate--liga-privada-10-seleccion-d.description: Announced in 2023 for markets outside the United States, this Liga Privada uses a lighter, rosado Connecticut Criollo wrapper over a Mexican binder, with Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania filler. The name recalls an old practice of sorting wrapper leaf for market. Milder than the Aniversario, it holds steady around black coffee, cedar and pepper.

thirds.notes: Black coffee and earth lead, with black pepper, cedar and a little cream behind.
Cedar moves up beside the coffee; toasted cream and pepper sit in the background.
Cedar and pepper take the lead, with earth, a lingering cream and a lightly charred finish.

sources.title: Drew Estate – Liga Privada 10 Selección de Mercado
Cigar Dojo – Liga Privada 10 Selección de Mercado announcement
Cigar Coop – Liga Privada 10 Selección de Mercado Toro review
Blind Man's Puff – Liga Privada 10 Selección de Mercado

drew-estate--liga-privada-unico-serie.description: A limited Liga Privada series of one-off blends and shapes, each built as a distinct, hard-hitting experiment. Some use the T52 Habano wrapper (Dirty Rat, Ratzilla, L40), others the No. 9 Broadleaf (Year of the Rat, Velvet Rat, Feral Flying Pig). Strength and flavour differ by vitola, from creamy to very full.

sources.title: Drew Estate – Liga Privada Único Serie

drew-estate--liga-privada-papas-fritas.description: A short-filler Liga Privada, made from the trimmings of the Liga blends, hand-sorted and cut to a uniform size, then rolled under a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper with a Brazilian Mata Fina binder. It is built as a half-hour smoke. Wood, leather and cocoa lead, and the strength climbs quickly toward the end.

thirds.notes: Wood and leather in front, cocoa behind, and black pepper through the nose.
The same core grows sweeter and more intense.
Pepper and spice sharpen over leather and cocoa as the strength reaches full.

sources.title: Drew Estate – Liga Privada Papas Fritas
Cigars Lover – Liga Privada Único Serie Papas Fritas

drew-estate--undercrown-maduro.description: Created in 2010 by the rollers at Drew Estate's Estelí factory when Liga Privada was too scarce for them to smoke. A Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper covers a stalk-cut Connecticut Habano binder and Brazilian Mata Fina and Nicaraguan filler. Earthy and naturally sweet, it moves through leather and char toward coffee and pepper.

thirds.notes: Sweet at first, then earth and leather with a grilled, charred note and red pepper on the nose.
Charcoal and leather, with coffee arriving near the midpoint and the pepper building.
Coffee leads to the nub, with leather and steady pepper.

sources.title: The Cigar Authority – Undercrown Maduro Belicoso review

drew-estate--undercrown-shade.description: Released in 2015 as the lighter companion to Undercrown Maduro, again developed by the factory rollers. An Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper covers a Sumatra binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. It smokes creamy and balanced, with caramel-like sweetness, vanilla and hay over earth, and suits a morning or early afternoon.

thirds.notes: Buttery caramel sweetness with soft vanilla, and hay and earth on the retrohale.
The sweetness carries on, then the smoke turns mainly earthy with a longer, hay-like finish.
Earth and hay remain, with a touch of coffee and a returning sweetness.

sources.title: The Cigar Authority – Undercrown Shade Gran Toro review

drew-estate--undercrown-10.description: Released in 2021 for ten years of Undercrown, this blend reverses the usual order: a dark Mexican San Andrés Negro wrapper over a Connecticut Broadleaf binder, with Nicaraguan and Honduran filler. It is dense and dark, with espresso, bitter chocolate, dried cherry and black pepper, and an earthy, cedar close.

thirds.notes: Espresso and black pepper first, then dark chocolate and dried cherry on the retrohale.
Leather and oak join the espresso and chocolate; the pepper softens into a creamy sweetness.
Espresso and chocolate deepen, with earth and cedar on a long finish.

drew-estate--undercrown-el-tigre-dominic.description: Launched in April 2026, the first Dominican-led Undercrown: Dominican HVA and Criollo '98 filler, an H99 Connecticut Corojo binder and an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, soft box-pressed and rolled at La Gran Fábrica in Nicaragua. Drew Estate describes a medium-full smoke of white pepper, roasted espresso and earth with a smooth, silky spice.

sources.title: Drew Estate – Undercrown El Tigre Dominicano
Cigar Dojo – Undercrown goes Dominican with El Tigre

drew-estate--herrera-esteli-habano.description: The first blend Willy Herrera made as Drew Estate's master blender, released in 2014 after more than seventy trial blends. An Ecuadorian Habano wrapper covers a Honduran binder and Nicaraguan filler, in a Cuban-leaning style. White pepper, cedar and nutmeg open, then the smoke turns sweeter, with cocoa and oak.

thirds.notes: White pepper and cedar with nutmeg-like spice and a nutty, toasty undertone.
The pepper eases; cinnamon, cocoa and a little coffee appear as cedar turns to oak.
Darker, with cocoa to the fore and the spice coming back.

sources.title: Stogie Press – Herrera Estelí Toro Especial review
Best Cigar Prices – Herrera Estelí Robusto Extra review

drew-estate--herrera-esteli-brazilian-ma.description: Introduced in 2018, this Herrera Estelí blend pairs a Brazilian Mata Fina maduro wrapper with a Connecticut River Valley Broadleaf binder and Nicaraguan and Dominican filler. Cocoa and coffee lead, with a floral touch and cedar, and a red pepper that grows on the retrohale as the strength rises.

thirds.notes: Hot cocoa and creamy coffee, with cedar and a little red pepper behind.
Sweetness fades; cedar, earth and floral notes rise and the pepper gets heavy on the nose.
Cedar and pepper lead, with coffee and earth beneath.

sources.title: Drew Estate – Herrera Estelí Brazilian Maduro
Cigar Coop – Herrera Estelí Brazilian Maduro Toro Especial review
The Cigar Authority – Herrera Estelí Brazilian Maduro review

drew-estate--nica-rustica-broadleaf.description: The original Nica Rustica, a tribute to the tobacco town of Estelí, where Drew Estate opened its factory in 1998. A Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper covers a Mexican San Andrés Negro binder and Nicaraguan filler from Estelí and Jalapa. Earthy and rustic, with roasted coffee, dry wood, hay and a mild spice.

thirds.notes: Soil-like earth and roasted coffee bean, with a sweetened hay note.
Drier and woodier, with hay, baking spice and a little red pepper on the retrohale.
Smooth to the end, tapering toward leather, campfire earth and a touch of cocoa.

sources.title: Blind Man's Puff – Nica Rustica El Brujito

drew-estate--nica-rustica-adobe.description: Released in 2022 as the second Nica Rustica, named for the adobe barrios of Estelí. A Habano wrapper covers a Brazilian binder and Nicaraguan filler from Estelí and Jalapa. Mellow to medium, it opens on lively pepper and thick, creamy smoke, then turns warmer and sweeter, with cocoa and nuts.

thirds.notes: Bright pepper over creamy smoke, giving way to a light fruit note.
Savoury spice and cream, with cocoa and a sweet, nutty aroma.
Spice carries the close with little further change.

sources.title: Stogie Press – Nica Rustica Adobe Gordo review

drew-estate--nica-rustica-shade.description: The mildest Nica Rustica, wrapped in Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade over a Mexican binder, with filler from Nicaragua, the United States and the Dominican Republic. Drew Estate describes it as mellow and relaxed, with a buttery core and light hints of wood, a calm choice for the morning.

drew-estate--blackened-m81.description: The first Blackened release, made with James Hetfield and master distiller Rob Dietrich; M81 nods to 1981, the year Metallica formed. A Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper covers a Connecticut River Broadleaf binder, with Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania filler. Dark and dense, with chocolate, wood, leather and black pepper.

thirds.notes: Semi-sweet chocolate and wood, with black pepper and earth.
Leather grows beside chocolate and wood, with a nutty note and a little cinnamon.
Leather and coffee close it out, with a bitter edge and quieter pepper.

sources.title: The Cigar Authority – Blackened M81 Robusto review

drew-estate--blackened-s84.description: The second Blackened blend, revealed in 2024, keeps the dark M81 core of Connecticut River Broadleaf binder and Nicaraguan and Pennsylvania filler, but trades the maduro wrapper for Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade. The smoke is velvety: coffee and cream at first, then cedar and wood with a gentle black pepper.

thirds.notes: Coffee and cream almost like café au lait, with cedar, honey and hay.
The cream fades as cedar and wood build; pepper and roasted nut appear.
Cedar and wood take over, with pepper returning and coffee underneath.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Blackened S84 Shade to Black Toro review
Blind Man's Puff – Blackened S84 Toro

drew-estate--20-acre-farm.description: Made with Jeff Borysiewicz of Corona Cigar Co. to showcase tobacco from his twenty-acre farm in Clermont, Florida, part of an effort to revive Florida-grown leaf. Connecticut Shade wraps a Connecticut River Valley Habano binder and Nicaraguan and Florida Sun Grown filler. Creamy and smooth, with cedar, oak, nuts and a hint of orange.

thirds.notes: Buttery cream with cedar, white pepper and nuts on the retrohale.
White pepper continues with mild oak and a toasted-bread note.
Smooths out into sweet cedar, nuts and a caramel-like sweetness.

sources.title: Blind Man's Puff – 20 Acre Farm Toro
Cigar Obsession – 20 Acre Farm Toro review

drew-estate--factory-smokes-maduro.description: A budget, factory-direct Drew Estate line, presented as a tribute to working smokers, with an Indonesian binder and Central American filler. The Maduro version wears a dark maduro wrapper and smokes medium, dark and smooth, with coffee, earth, spice and a little black pepper; an easy everyday cigar.

sources.title: Casas Fumando – Factory Smokes Maduro review
Gotham Cigars – Factory Smokes by Drew Estate review

thirds.notes: Earthy and slightly gritty, with cocoa on the finish and a mild pepper.
Still earthy, with more pepper and a meatier, medium-weight smoke.
A yeasty note joins earth and pepper, and a warming spice builds toward the end.

drew-estate--factory-smokes-sweet.description: A budget, factory-direct Drew Estate line, presented as a tribute to working smokers, with an Indonesian binder and Central American filler. The Sweet version has a sweetened cap on a Habano wrapper and smokes mellow and creamy, with coffee and vanilla.

drew-estate--factory-smokes-shade.description: A budget, factory-direct Drew Estate line, presented as a tribute to working smokers, with an Indonesian binder and Central American filler. The Shade version wears a Connecticut Shade wrapper and smokes mellow and creamy, with cedar, butter and a slight pepper note.

drew-estate--factory-smokes-sun-grown.description: A budget, factory-direct Drew Estate line, presented as a tribute to working smokers, with an Indonesian binder and Central American filler. The Sun Grown version wears a sun-grown Habano wrapper and smokes medium, warm and spicy, with baking spice, cinnamon and a natural sweetness.

sources.title: Drew Estate – Factory Smokes Sun Grown

drew-estate--acid-blue.description: Part of ACID, the infused range Drew Estate started in 1996, made with curing and blending methods kept private at La Gran Fábrica in Nicaragua. Blue, the original ACID line, is mellow and smooth, with a sweet, herbal and aromatic smoke, in sizes from the small Krush to the Kuba Kuba and the 6 x 60 Kuba Grande.

sources.title: JR Cigars Blending Room – ACID Kuba Kuba review
Cigar Place – ACID Kuba Kuba review
LM Cigars – ACID Kuba Kuba review

thirds.notes: A sweet, botanical start with floral and vanilla tones that settles onto cedar, leather and earth, with a sharp spice early on.
The infusion eases a little as dried fruit, leather and cedar come through, with warm spice and a grassy, earthy edge.
The same core holds to the end, earthier and spicier, while a sugary sweetness stays on the lips.

drew-estate--acid-gold.description: Part of ACID, the infused range Drew Estate started in 1996, made with curing and blending methods kept private at La Gran Fábrica in Nicaragua. Gold is a separate blend with its own golden, sweet aroma, offered as the Krush Gold, Blondie Gold, Atom Maduro and the slim Cold Infusion.

drew-estate--acid-morado.description: Part of ACID, the infused range Drew Estate started in 1996, made with curing and blending methods kept private at La Gran Fábrica in Nicaragua. Morado, the purple ACID, uses hand-selected Nicaraguan tobacco with a deep infusion and a rich, juicy bouquet, from the Croqueta and Krush Purple up to the Extra Ordinary Larry.

drew-estate--acid-green.description: Part of ACID, the infused range Drew Estate started in 1996, made with curing and blending methods kept private at La Gran Fábrica in Nicaragua. Green uses a candela wrapper, the green leaf that was America's most common wrapper until the early 1980s, and smokes mellow, grassy, earthy and herbal.

drew-estate--acid-20.description: Part of ACID, the infused range Drew Estate started in 1996, made with curing and blending methods kept private at La Gran Fábrica in Nicaragua. ACID 20 marks the brand's first twenty years, with a sweet, aromatic infusion and warm spice, in a box-pressed Maduro Robusto, a Maduro Toro and a Connecticut Toro.

thirds.notes: Sweet and floral from the infusion, over an earthy base with leather and cedar or cocoa, and a little pepper through the nose.
Mellower, with soil, herbal and floral notes and a fruity, orange-like sweetness; pepper grows on the retrohale.
Warm earth and a touch more pepper lead the close; the infusion returns strongly in some sizes and fades in others.

drew-estate--acid-subculture.description: Part of ACID, the infused range Drew Estate started in 1996, made with curing and blending methods kept private at La Gran Fábrica in Nicaragua. Subculture is a series of small-batch infused blends for dedicated ACID smokers, made from limited, higher-grade tobaccos.

drew-estate--tabak-especial-dulce.description: Drew Estate's coffee cigar, made since 2002 by pairing roasted coffee with dark-air-cured tobacco, a blend worked out with a master barista over several years. Dulce, modelled on café con leche, wraps Nicaraguan filler and a Sumatra binder in Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade, and smokes mellow, with coffee, cream and milk chocolate.

sources.title: After Action Cigars – Tabak Especial Dulce review

thirds.notes: Sweet coffee and milk chocolate, with creamy tobacco in the background.
The sweetness eases and the coffee turns softer and milkier, with the chocolate coming and going.
Cocoa and an espresso-like coffee take over as the sweetness fades, smooth to the finish.

drew-estate--tabak-especial-negra.description: Drew Estate's coffee cigar, made since 2002 by pairing roasted coffee with dark-air-cured tobacco, a blend worked out with a master barista over several years. Negra uses a two-year-aged San Andrés maduro wrapper over a Sumatra binder and Nicaraguan filler, with a dark-roast character of earth, chocolate and espresso.

sources.title: After Action Cigars – Tabak Especial Negra review
Casas Fumando – Tabak Especial Toro Negra review

thirds.notes: Sweet coffee and milk chocolate over an earthy tobacco base, with cedar and cocoa on the aroma.
The sweetness eases and leather, nutty and toasty notes join the coffee, while the strength holds steady.
Espresso becomes the main note, the chocolate falls back and a light sweetness stays to the end.

drew-estate--isla-del-sol-maduro.description: A coffee-paired Drew Estate line co-created with Tommy Sullivan, combining Sumatra Mandheling coffee with Nicaraguan dark-air-cured tobacco. The Maduro wears a San Andrés maduro wrapper over Indonesian binder and Indonesian and Nicaraguan filler, and smokes mellow and chocolatey, with coffee and mocha.

sources.title: Drew Estate – Isla del Sol Maduro

drew-estate--isla-del-sol-sun-grown.description: A coffee-paired Drew Estate line co-created with Tommy Sullivan, combining Sumatra Mandheling coffee with Nicaraguan dark-air-cured tobacco. The Sun Grown wears a sun-grown Sumatra wrapper over Indonesian binder and Indonesian and Nicaraguan filler, and smokes mellow and smooth, with coffee and a gentle sweetness.

sources.title: Drew Estate – Isla del Sol Sun Grown

drew-estate--kentucky-fire-cured-origina.description: Built on Kentucky tobacco that is fire-cured over hardwood smoke, a curing method used there for more than two centuries, blended with Nicaraguan leaf. The Original has a double wrapper, Kentucky Tapa Negra at the head and San Andrés at the foot, over a Connecticut Shade binder. It smokes medium, with hickory, oak and maple.

sources.title: Drew Estate – Kentucky Fire Cured Original
Klaro Cigars – Kentucky Fire Cured (Fat Molly) review
Cigar Czars – Kentucky Fire Cured Fat Molly review

thirds.notes: Malty and earthy, with dark chocolate, dried cherry and black pepper, and a smoky, maple-like sweetness on the retrohale.
Smoother and creamier, with nuts and mocha as the smokiness briefly steps back.
Nuttiness leads, the wood smoke returns, and the cigar turns drier and a little bolder.

drew-estate--kentucky-fire-cured-sweet.description: Built on Kentucky tobacco that is fire-cured over hardwood smoke, a curing method used there for more than two centuries, blended with Nicaraguan leaf. The Sweet version adds a sweetened cap to a San Andrés wrapper over a Connecticut Shade binder. It is mellow and smoky-sweet, with savoury notes recalling maple bacon, bourbon and barbecue.

sources.title: Drew Estate – Kentucky Fire Cured Sweet

drew-estate--pappy-van-winkle-barrel-fer.description: Made with Pappy & Company and the Van Winkle family: Kentucky tobacco is fire-cured, then fermented in retired Pappy Van Winkle bourbon barrels in St. James Parish, Louisiana. That leaf covers an Indonesian wrapper and binder, with fire-cured and Nicaraguan filler. Medium, with charred oak, a peaty smokiness and burnt coffee.

sources.title: Drew Estate – Pappy Van Winkle Barrel Fermented
Cigar Coop – Pappy Van Winkle Barrel Fermented Churchill review

thirds.notes: Mocha and cedar trade places with a bourbon-like sweetness of charred wood and caramel, with campfire char on the retrohale.
The bourbon-barrel sweetness moves to the front, now and then with a sour edge, as mocha and cedar recede.
Earth joins the sweetness, cedar grows again and a little mocha lingers to the end.

drew-estate--pappy-van-winkle-tradition.description: A blend Willy Herrera created in 2012, chosen by Julian P. Van Winkle III for the Pappy & Company range. An Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro wrapper covers a premium Indonesian binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. A traditional, unflavoured cigar, full and smooth, with chocolate, earth, leather and nuts.

sources.title: Drew Estate – Pappy Van Winkle Tradition
The Cigar Authority – Pappy Van Winkle Tradition Belicoso Fino review
Cigar Inspector – Pappy Van Winkle Tradition Coronita review
Stogie Review – Pappy Van Winkle Tradition Belicoso Fino

thirds.notes: Sweet and leathery, with pepper, a rye-like spice and hints of hay, earth and wood; caramel is strong in the first inch.
The sweetness deepens, with cinnamon, raisin, a first hint of dark chocolate and leather toward the end.
Chocolate and leather lead, with cedar, a little pepper and a creamy vanilla note as the finish shortens.

drew-estate--deadwood-sweet-jane.description: Part of the Deadwood Tobacco Co. range, named for the South Dakota gold-rush town, where each blend honours one of the town's 'Vixens'. Sweet Jane was the first, a 5 x 46 corona now also sold as a 4 x 32 tin. Under a maduro wrapper it smokes mellow and sweet, with coffee, cedar and chocolate.

drew-estate--deadwood-fat-bottom-betty.description: Part of the Deadwood Tobacco Co. range, named for the South Dakota gold-rush town, where each blend honours one of the town's 'Vixens'. Fat Bottom Betty has a maduro wrapper over an undisclosed blend and smokes medium to full, with wood, leather, black pepper and dark-roast coffee around a sweet core.

sources.title: Drew Estate – Deadwood Fat Bottom Betty
JR Cigars Blending Room – Fat Bottom Betty review
Cigar Place – Deadwood Fat Bottom Betty review

thirds.notes: Sweetness from the cap with black pepper and nutmeg, then wood and leather; another taster found chocolate, coffee and vanilla.
Dark-roast coffee and cinnamon come through as the sweetness eases, with earth, a little nuttiness and pepper on the retrohale.
Baking spice carries to the end, and chocolate, coffee and a creamy sweetness return.

drew-estate--deadwood-crazy-alice.description: Part of the Deadwood Tobacco Co. range, named for the South Dakota gold-rush town, where each blend honours one of the town's 'Vixens'. Crazy Alice is a short, shaped maduro, about four inches long with a ring that runs from 38 to 52. It smokes medium to full, with cocoa, roasted coffee, earth and dried fruit.

drew-estate--deadwood-leather-rose.description: Part of the Deadwood Tobacco Co. range, named for the South Dakota gold-rush town, where each blend honours one of the town's 'Vixens'. Leather Rose, a maduro in a 4 x 43 petite corona and a 5 x 54 torpedo, is a full-bodied blend, with cedar, oak, white pepper, earth and a quiet sweetness.

sources.title: Best Cigar Prices – Deadwood Leather Rose review
After Action Cigars – Deadwood Leather Rose review

thirds.notes: The sweet tip leads, with cream, cedar, cocoa and vanilla, and a light pepper on the finish.
As the sweetness recedes, creamy leather comes forward with coffee, steady cocoa and a touch of white pepper.
The fullest part: espresso, earth, chocolate and leather, with white pepper and a fading sweetness.

drew-estate--deadwood-the-girl-with-no-n.description: Part of the Deadwood Tobacco Co. range, named for the South Dakota gold-rush town, where each blend honours one of the town's 'Vixens'. The Girl With No Name is a 7 x 44 lonsdale under a Mexican San Andrés wrapper, sold in retailer-exclusive editions; strength and flavour vary by vitola.

sources.title: Drew Estate – Deadwood The Girl With No Name

drew-estate--deadwood-dominicana.description: Part of the Deadwood Tobacco Co. range, named for the South Dakota gold-rush town, where each blend honours one of the town's 'Vixens'. Dominicana was the first Dominican-led blend rolled at La Gran Fábrica: Dominican filler, a San Andrés binder and a Connecticut Shade wrapper with a sweet cap. Mellow to medium, with figs, hay, honey, cream and a buttery finish.

drew-estate--deadwood-dominicana-buenas-.description: Part of the Deadwood Tobacco Co. range, named for the South Dakota gold-rush town, where each blend honours one of the town's 'Vixens'. Buenas Noches is the darker evening companion to Dominicana, with the same Dominican-led filler and San Andrés binder under a sweet-capped Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. Mellow to medium, with cocoa, earth and warm spice.

sources.title: Drew Estate – Deadwood Dominicana Buenas Noches

drew-estate--the-egg.description: An egg-shaped cigar first sold in Drew Estate's early Natural Aqua Systems days, when the company began at a small kiosk in the World Trade Center. It swells past 100 ring at the centre and tapers at both ends. The Connecticut is creamy, then peppery with oak; the Maduro brings dark cocoa and espresso.
